Modern Design
THE MEASURE OF
GREATNESS.
We’ll save you from breaking out the yardstick: Tucson has up to 55.8
cubic feet of rear cargo space, and more passenger volume than the 2014
Ford Escape. Two-stage reclining 60/40 split rear seats add even more
passenger comfort and storage versatility.
An available navigation system with NavTraffic® adds convenience to your
comfort with a large 7˝ touchscreen display that’s easy to read at a glance.1
The center console display is also your portal to Hyundai Blue Link – a
suite of infotainment, safety and service features that brings some of the
best things about living in this digital age along for the ride.
For 2015, a new Popular Equipment Package on Tucson GLS bundles
leatherette-trimmed seats, a power driver’s seat with power lumbar,
automatic headlight control and a 4.3˝ color audio display that also serves
as a monitor for the rearview camera.

Distinctive Engineering
GIVE YOUR RIDE AN
INTELLIGENCE TEST.
When you’re out for a test drive, be sure to do a U-turn in the vehicle
you’re evaluating. How well it does is a sign of intelligent engineering.
Spoiler alert: Tucson’s turning radius is more than 2 feet tighter than the
2014 Honda CR-V. That’s sure to make parallel parking in tight spaces a
whole lot easier. Making you look a whole lot smarter.
Tucson is clever enough to outmaneuver gas stations, too. An advanced
technology called Gasoline Direct Injection makes our engines some of the
most powerful in their class – while still achieving remarkable fuel economy.
The standard 2.0L engine delivers 164 HP with an EPA-estimated 29
MPG highway rating. The available 2.4L powerplant, 182 HP with an
EPA-estimated 28 MPG highway rating.1

driving practices. No system, no matter how advanced, can overcome physics or correct poor driving.
The driver is always responsible for controlling the vehicle and must use caution to avoid loss of control
in all driving conditions. Speed, road conditions and driver steering input will affect whether ESC can help
prevent loss of control. See Owner’s Manual for details. The Traction Control System is meant to enhance
conscientious driving habits and is not a substitute for safe driving practices.
